title: Kernel based quantum machine learning at record rate : Many-body distribution functionals as compact representations

metadata.authors: Khan, Danish; Heinen, Stefan; von Lilienfeld, O. Anatole

source_summary: The study introduces compact, linear-scaling quantum machine learning representations based on atomic Gaussian many-body distribution functionals, achieving competitive predictive performance and data efficiency for chemical property prediction while significantly reducing computational costs compared to high-dimensional feature mappings.
abstract: The feature vector mapping used to represent chemical systems is a key factor governing the superior data-efficiency of kernel based quantum machine learning (QML) models applicable throughout chemical compound space. Unfortunately, the most accurate representations require a high dimensional feature mapping, thereby imposing a considerable computational burden on model training and use. We introduce compact yet accurate, linear scaling QML representations based on atomic Gaussian many-body distribution functionals (MBDF), and their derivatives. Weighted density functions (DF) of MBDF values are used as global representations which are constant in size, i.e.~invariant with respect to the number of atoms. We report predictive performance and training data efficiency that is competitive with state of the art for two diverse datasets of organic molecules, QM9 and QMugs. Generalization capability has been investigated for atomization energies, HOMO-LUMO eigenvalues and gap, internal energies at 0 K, zero point vibrational energies, dipole moment norm, static isotropic polarizability, and heat capacity as encoded in QM9. MBDF based QM9 performance lowers the optimal Pareto front spanned between sampling and training cost to compute node minutes,~effectively sampling chemical compound space with chemical accuracy at a sampling rate of $\sim 48$ molecules per core second.

methods.value: Introduced MBDF and density of functionals (DF) representations, tested on QM9 and QMugs datasets using kernel ridge regression (KRR).

problems.value: The high dimensional feature mapping required for accurate quantum machine learning (QML) models imposes a significant computational burden.

hypotheses.value: Compact yet accurate linear scaling QML representations based on atomic Gaussian many-body distribution functionals (MBDF) can achieve competitive predictive performance and training data efficiency.

evidence.value: MBDF/DF representations demonstrated predictive performance competitive with state-of-the-art, with significantly reduced computational cost and time complexity.

conclusions.value: MBDF/DF representations can accurately describe any atom/molecule using a minimal number of discrete elements, thereby reducing QML training and prediction times by multiple orders of magnitude for small and large molecules.
